rules.name: Insufficient Flow Control Mechanisms
rules.description: Lack of enforcement of security checks or approvals (e.g. branch protection, required reviews) in the pipeline. Attackers can push malicious code without review.

rules.name: Inadequate Identity and Access Management
rules.description: Overly permissive access to the CI/CD systems, allowing unauthorized code changes or exfiltration of secrets.

rules.name: Dependency Chain Abuse
rules.description: Exploiting flaws in how dependencies are fetched (e.g., Dependency Confusion, Typosquatting) to inject malicious packages into the build.

rules.name: Poisoned Pipeline Execution (PPE)
rules.description: Attackers modify the CI configuration file or build scripts to execute malicious commands during the build process.

rules.name: Insufficient Pipeline-Based Access Controls (PBAC)
rules.description: Pipelines running with overly broad permissions, allowing a compromised build to steal credentials, move laterally, or alter production infrastructure.

rules.name: Insufficient Credential Hygiene
rules.description: Hardcoded secrets, shared credentials, exposed logs, and unrotated tokens in CI/CD systems give attackers easy access to high-value systems.

rules.name: Insecure System Configuration
rules.description: Poor network controls, default credentials, weak hardening, and insecure settings in CI/CD infrastructure may allow lateral movement or access to secrets.

rules.name: Ungoverned Usage of 3rd Party Services
rules.description: Uncontrolled integration of third-party services and dependencies into the CI/CD ecosystem, expanding the attack surface without proper vetting.

rules.name: Improper Artifact Integrity Validation
rules.description: Lack of verification that build artifacts have not been tampered with between build and deployment, enabling supply-chain injection of malicious code.

rules.name: Insufficient Logging and Visibility
rules.description: Lack of centralized, comprehensive logging across CI/CD systems prevents timely detection and investigation of security incidents.
